gloss: way of taking something (mentally); interpretation; reaction

definitions.gloss: way of taking (something said or done); way of interpreting; way of reacting to
definitions.explanation: How a person mentally or emotionally takes in something — news, criticism, an event, or another person's words. Emphasizes that different people may react or interpret things in different ways.

examples.japanese: {受|う}け{止|と}め{方|かた}が{違|ちが}う。
{人|ひと}によってニュースの{受|う}け{止|と}め{方|かた}はさまざまだ。
examples.english: People take the news in all sorts of different ways.

examples.japanese: {同|おな}じ{言葉|ことば}でも、{受|う}け{止|と}め{方|かた}{次第|しだい}で{傷|きず}つくこともある。
examples.english: Even the same words can hurt depending on how you take them.

examples.japanese: {先生|せんせい}の{注意|ちゅうい}を{素直|すなお}に{受|う}け{止|と}められるかどうかは、その{子|こ}の{受|う}け{止|と}め{方|かた}{次第|しだい}だ。
examples.english: Whether a child can take the teacher's advice in good faith depends on how that child reacts to it.

notes:
Composed of {受|う}け{止|と}める (to catch, receive; to take in or come to terms with) and the suffix ～{方|かた} (way of, manner of). The verb {受|う}け{止|と}める originally means to catch a ball or other physical thing, but is overwhelmingly used figuratively for taking in news, criticism, reality, or emotions.

USAGE:
Commonly used in discussions about communication, interpretation, and differing perspectives. Emphasizes the subjective side — how the listener or observer takes something, rather than the objective message.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {受|う}け{止|と}め{方|かた}が{違|ちが}う: the way of taking it differs
- {受|う}け{止|と}め{方|かた}{次第|しだい}: depending on how one takes it
- {人|ひと}それぞれの{受|う}け{止|と}め{方|かた}: each person's own way of taking it
- {国民|こくみん}の{受|う}け{止|と}め{方|かた}: the public's reaction (often in news commentary)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {受|う}け{取|と}り{方|かた}: way of receiving/interpreting — very close in meaning; slightly more neutral and often used for physical or literal interpretation
- {解釈|かいしゃく}: interpretation — emphasizes analytical, deliberate interpretation
- {捉|とら}え{方|かた}: way of grasping/perceiving — emphasizes how one conceptualizes something
- {感|かん}じ{方|かた}: way of feeling — emphasizes emotional reaction rather than mental interpretation
